hook_text: A baby born in Japan can expect to live about eighty-four years. In some war-torn countries, the figure is under sixty. Why?
clip_script: Wealth buys good food, clean water, vaccines and hospitals. So in rich countries, few babies die and people live into their eighties, and families are small. In poorer places, more children die young, and families are often bigger. Now add war. Bombs and bullets kill, but destroyed farms, clinics and water pipes often kill even more, through hunger and disease. And war sends people running: today over a hundred and ten million people are forced from their homes, most of them sheltering in a neighbouring country. Peace and development are population issues.
visual_style: Two side-by-side life expectancy bars grow to different heights; a calm village scene shifts to a damaged clinic; arrows of people move across a border into a camp.
pacing: Measured comparison, then a heavier middle, then a clear closing line.
